- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to under-forecast; adjust forecast upward by 1–2% of recent mean.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.67), model tends to over-forecast; adjust downward by 1–2% of recent mean.
- Model consistently under-responds to sharp upward sentiment spikes; if sentiment jumps >0.80 within 3 days, add 0.5–1.5% to forecast horizon.
- Model over-anticipates downward moves after negative sentiment; if sentiment drops below 0.33, reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% for next 3–5 days.
- Model exhibits mean reversion bias: if 3–5 consecutive days show downward trend, forecast should not drop below 10% below recent 7-day low.
- For 30-day horizon, model often underestimates late-period spikes (last 7–10 days); apply 1–3% upward bias if sentiment is rising and price is trending up.
- If sentiment history shows alternating high/low cycles, model tends to lag; add 0.5–1.0% to forecast for each cycle shift detected.
